data.hypothesis: Assigning one 32-lane warp to each output particle parallelizes the source scan and reduces the three force components with warp shuffles. With 256 threads per block, items_per_block=8 matches the eight output-owning warps. This may shorten the serial source traversal for the larger cases; the tree reduction changes floating-point summation order, so correctness must be checked before interpreting timing.
data.notes: Each warp shares one output index; lanes scan source indices lane, lane+32, and so on, skip self-interaction, and safely stop at n. Lane zero alone writes the copied particle, preserving its mass. The source reduction order differs from the baseline. No candidate correctness or timing result is available here; the supplied baseline-e1 result is valid at a mean of 0.0018545204 seconds, but has no per-size breakdown. Controller validation should precede timing comparison.
transformations: Replaced one-thread-per-output serial source traversal with one 32-lane warp per output; each lane accumulates a strided source subset and the warp reduces force components using __shfl_down_sync.

Configured 256 threads and 8 output items per block, matching one output per warp; guarded output/source tails, skipped self-interactions, and restricted writes to lane zero while copying the original particle mass.
